To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the brain of a typical fish yields subcellular fractions, including a well‐defined fraction of synaptosomes, similar to those previously described in higher forms.

synaptosomes can be isolated from the brain of a teleost fish, the sea bass (Centropristis striatus), and that the synaptosomal preparation contains a high proportion of acetylcholine‐releasing nerve terminals.

(1) the brain of a teleost fish, Centriopristes striatus, yields subcellular fractions that are very similar to those previously obtained from mammalian brain; (2) a well-defined synaptosomal fraction is obtained that accounts for most of the tissue-bound acetylcholine; (3) this synaptosomal fraction may not be as pure as that obtained from mammalian brains due to the presence of a relatively large amount of myeline in teleost brains;
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of a synaptosomal fraction from brain tissue.
the isolation of subcellular fractions from brain tissue, with particular emphasis on the isolation of synaptosomal fractions.
the isolation and characterization of synaptosomes from the brain of the sea bass.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synapses in the teleost are similar to those of higher vertebrates, in that the synapse is a functional unit and that the presynaptic terminal is a sealed vesicle‐containing structure.
the synaptic apparatus of the brain of a teleost fish is essentially similar to that of a mammal, and that the synapses of the former are capable of being isolated in the intact state.

the brain of a teleost fish is similar to that of higher vertebrates in its subcellular organization and that the methods used in the isolation of synaptosomal fractions from the latter are equally applicable to the former.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although the brain of a fish is structurally quite different from that of a mammal in many respects, its synaptic apparatus is essentially the same in its fundamental properties.

synapses of the teleost brain, like those of the mammalian brain, have a high degree of structural organization, and that the methods used to study the structure, chemistry, and physiology of the mammalian synapse are adaptable to the study of the teleost synapse.
the synapses of teleosts, at least of the type found in their central nervous system, are not unique but have the same physical and chemical properties as those found in the brains of higher forms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
synaptosomes are present in the brain of a teleost fish.
the synapse is a fundamental unit of brain function.
the isolation of synaptosomal preparations from teleost fish brain is feasible.
